Implemented in [output/main.py](/workspace/output/main.py).

What’s included:

- Full CLI contract:
  - `--bib`, `--style`, `--output`
  - `--cites` and/or `--aux` (at least one required)
  - `--log` optional
- `.bib` parser:
  - `@entry`, `@string`, `@preamble`, `@comment`
  - `{}` and `()` delimiters
  - `#` concatenation, numeric/braced/quoted/macro operands
  - predefined month macros + user override
  - duplicate-key detection and warnings
  - cited-key selection (case-insensitive match, preserved key casing)
  - crossref inheritance (non-transitive) with unresolved/cycle warnings
- `.bst` parser + stack-machine interpreter:
  - top-level commands (`ENTRY`, `FUNCTION`, `MACRO`, `READ`, `EXECUTE`, `ITERATE`, `REVERSE`, `SORT`, `INTEGERS`, `STRINGS`)
  - function literals, quoted names, integer/string literals, operators
  - built-ins needed by canonical styles (`plain/alpha/unsrt/abbrv`), including `format.name$`, `purify$`, `change.case$`, `text.prefix$`, `text.length$`, `width$`, etc.
- `.bbl` output writer:
  - `write$`/`newline$` behavior
  - 79-column wrapping with continuation indent
  - LF line endings, UTF-8
  - end-of-run flush
- JSON outputs:
  - success log schema (`--log`)
  - failure JSON in `--output` with required shape
  - warning objects with canonical `kind` strings
- Exit codes:
  - `0` success
  - `1` parse/load/runtime contract failures
  - `2` unexpected internal failures

I also ran smoke tests against all four canonical styles to verify end-to-end execution and output generation.
